caption: A pot of pasta water boils over on a stove, and foamy water spills down the outside of the pot onto the burner.

sa.check: A pot sits on a stove.
Foam rises inside the pot and over the rim.
Foamy water runs down the outside of the pot to the burner.
The water is pasta water: cloudy, starchy foam, pasta may be visible.
The order is foam rises, spills over, runs down.

pc.expect: The foam climbs from inside the pot up and over the rim, and spilled foam is on its way down the outside: inside to out, up then over then down.
pc.fail: Foam climbs back up the outside into the pot; or the spill retreats over the rim; or the outside is wet before any foam reaches the rim.

pc.expect: Once over the rim the foam and water run downward on the pot wall and onto the burner.
pc.fail: Foam runs sideways round the pot or upward; or falls up; or hangs off the rim as a static curtain without descending.

pc.expect: The overflow is a frothy liquid: bubbles collapse, the liquid streaks, and it steams or spits on the hot burner.
pc.fail: The foam sits as a rigid dome that does not deform; or the spill behaves as a solid sheet peeling off; or the liquid on the hot burner lies still with no steam or reaction.

pc.expect: Foam over the rim means the level inside has reached the rim; the spill wets the pot wall and leaves it wet.
pc.fail: Foam pours over while the visible inside is calm and far from full; or the wall is dry again right after foam ran down it.

pc.expect: One pot that keeps its shape; foam passes only over the rim, not through the wall.
pc.fail: Foam appears on the outside with none crossing the rim; or the pot changes shape or size; or a second pot appears; or foam passes through the pot wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: Pot colour, stove knobs and burner layout stay the same.
pc.fail: The pot changes colour; or the burner moves; or the stovetop pattern changes.
